clue.text: Sergeant mostly seen in fleece

indicators.note: mostly tells you to use all but the final letter of the sergeant's name

parts.note: Sergeant Bilko is the scheming army con man of the 1950s American sitcom The Phil Silvers Show

explanation.surface: An army sergeant spends most of his time wrapped up in a warm fleece jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean to swindle or cheat someone out of money.

clue.text: Associated with two parties, oil company worker adopts one

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the company and worker together take the single letter inside

parts.note: BP is the British oil company, formerly British Petroleum
I is the Roman numeral for one
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: An oil company employee linked to two political parties formally joins one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something backed by both political sides, as in a cross-bench agreement.

clue.text: Imaginatively, rice contributes to this

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grain, used creatively, adds something to a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case rice also hints at Sir Tim Rice, the British writer of words for musicals, so the whole clue points at what 'this' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice writes the words of songs, so the thing he imaginatively adds to is a song's text.

clue.text: Suspect valid issue can be imagined

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not to be trusted, so the two words after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone believes that a legitimate problem is at least conceivable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a verb of belief in the surface but is the anagram signal for 'valid issue'; 'can be' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle synonym: something pictured in the mind's eye has been formed as a mental image.

clue.text: Sort of bakery coming in the future

definitions.meaning: a bakery sited inside a supermarket rather than on its own premises is described this way
what lies ahead for someone is said to be this, as in trouble awaiting them

explanation.surface: A new kind of bread shop is due to open before long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a bakery within a supermarket and, as an idiom, whatever awaits someone later.

clue.text: Sterling post office lost, therefore experience needed

indicators.note: lost says the post office's letters go missing from the word for the money

parts.note: sterling is British money, whose unit is the pound
ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English

explanation.surface: A first-rate post office has closed, so the job now calls for people with know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes PO out of POUND, leaving UND. 'experience' reads as a noun in the surface but defines as a verb; 'needed' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to go through or be subjected to something, as with surgery or a change.

clue.text: Tropical grasshopper, no tail in place

indicators.note: no tail means the insect's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a locust is a swarming grasshopper of hot countries

explanation.surface: A tailless tropical grasshopper sits just where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived noun for a particular position or site, used in mathematics and genetics.

clue.text: A softened composition is no good for person like this

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the two words before it are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentler piece of music is wasted on a certain kind of listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' reads as a piece of music but is the anagram signal for 'A softened'. The rest of the clue describes the answer: quiet music is useless to someone who cannot hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes someone wholly unable to hear, for whom quiet music would be useless.

clue.text: Does perhaps rush from south to north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going from south to north means the plant's name is read upwards

parts.note: a rush is a waterside plant much like a reed

explanation.surface: Someone possibly hurries northwards from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' wants to be the verb; it is the plural of doe. 'from south to north' turns REED upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Does are the females of this animal, whose plural is spelt like its singular; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Good chums around catch up immediately

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole assembled run is read from bottom to top
around places the first two pieces either side of the word for catch

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, as in school marks
pals are chums or friends
to nab someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: Kind friends gather round and bring someone up to date straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch up' reads as one phrase but splits between two jobs: 'around' wraps the good chums about the catch, and 'up' turns the resulting GNABPALS over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adverb meaning directly or all at once, without any delay.

clue.text: Work relays in block brought to a standstill

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the word for block

parts.note: a pad is a block of paper, as in a writing pad

indicators.note: work as an instruction means to knead or rework the letters of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Repairs to the electrical relays in an apartment block have ground to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work relays' looks like a maintenance job, but 'Work' is the anagram signal, making RALYSE, and 'in' is a real insertion into the block rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle synonym: something immobilised or halted completely, as a city by a strike.

clue.text: The end is nigh

definitions.meaning: the conclusion of something, as in the finish of a day's play

explanation.surface: A doom-monger's placard announces the apocalypse.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a conclusion or finish, and as an adjective it means near.

clue.text: Summary concerning the crown

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as at the head of a memo
a cap is the crown fitted on a tooth, and to crown something is to cap it

explanation.surface: A brief report about the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal noun for a brief restatement of the main points.

clue.text: Nothing new, heroin user's blighted careers

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament

indicators.note: blighted means ruined or spoiled, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: It's an old story: a heroin addict's working life has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blighted' rearranges H plus USERS into RUSHES. 'careers' reads as working lives but means headlong dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Careers as a noun can mean headlong dashes, and these are surges forward.

clue.text: Collapsed case of bloke clearly taking cocaine to be used again

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen apart, so the pieces that follow are jumbled together
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: taken as written
C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: The legal case against a man fell apart, though he was obviously on cocaine, and will be revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapsed' rearranges BE (the 'case of' bloke), CLEARLY and C; 'taking' only adds the C to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for material fit for reprocessing, such as glass or paper, rather than being thrown away.

clue.text: Tangier complex, one showing no appreciation

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In a Moroccan building development lives someone who is never grateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' reads as a noun, a group of buildings in the Moroccan city, but is the anagram signal for 'Tangier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an unthankful person, someone who gives no gratitude for kindness.

clue.text: Shellfish served up, party left with depression

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the whole run of three pieces is read upwards

parts.note: a do is an informal British word for a party
port is the left side of a ship
a sag is a dip or sunken place

explanation.surface: Seafood was dished up, and the guests went away feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the whole of DO PORT SAG over in this down entry; 'with' only joins the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails, whelks and limpets belong to this class of molluscs, so it is loosely a shelled sea creature.

clue.text: Outside broadcast display of emotion is repellent

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for outside broadcast, a programme made on location
to make a scene is to put on a public display of emotion

explanation.surface: A live television programme full of people emoting is off-putting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of disgusting or offensive to decency.

clue.text: What can be found on mountain tops? These!

parts.words: What can be found on mountain
parts.note: snow is what lies on a high mountain
caps are tops, as on bottles or pens

explanation.surface: A quiz question about high peaks, answered with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question does two jobs' worth of reading: split before 'tops' it gives the two pieces, and taken whole it describes what 'These!' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: These points back to the question: white coverings on summits are exactly what sits on mountain tops.

clue.text: Very Italian covering say, for spear made from wood

indicators.note: covering means the Italian word wraps around the short piece that follows

parts.note: assai is the Italian for very, seen in musical directions such as allegro assai
eg means for example, or say

explanation.surface: A thoroughly Italian sheath, for instance, protects a wooden spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender southern African throwing weapon, traditionally with a shaft cut from the tree of the same name.

clue.text: Your setter's finished with leader of opposition laying it on thick

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I'm, for your setter is
something finished is past, over

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is done with the opposition leader's exaggerated flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting technique in which paint is applied in heavy layers that stand out from the canvas.

clue.text: What may be swotted in usual offices in a cold manner?

indicators.note: in says the insect lives in the lavatory, so the room is named first, on the model of a house fly

parts.note: the usual offices is an old-fashioned British euphemism for the lavatory, here a loo
a fly is the insect one swats, and swot is a variant spelling of swat

explanation.surface: Something hit with a rolled newspaper in the lavatory, and without any warmth?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the pieces into an invented phrase on the model of 'a house fly'; the question mark admits the whimsy. 'Usual offices' is a British euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb for behaving distantly or with reserve, keeping others at arm's length.

clue.text: High tea entertaining celebrity goddess

indicators.note: entertaining means having as a guest inside, so the rearranged letters hold the celebrity
high can mean intoxicated and all over the place, so the drink's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous deity is the guest at a substantial early-evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: High tea is a British early-evening meal; here 'High' splits off as the anagram signal, making ATE, and 'entertaining' is the container holding the celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the Phoenician deity of fertility and love, the counterpart of Ishtar.

clue.text: Odd couple of drugs

parts.note: crack is a smokable form of cocaine, the first of the two drugs
pot is slang for cannabis, the second of the two drugs

explanation.surface: A mismatched pairing of two narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means eccentric or crazy, as said of a hare-brained scheme.

clue.text: Henry in cheap eatery gets something worth little

indicators.note: in puts Henry's single letter inside the word for the eatery

parts.note: caff is British slang for a cafe, especially a cheap one
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry is served something almost worthless at a greasy spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the husks separated from grain; figuratively anything of no value.

clue.text: Labour, both sides of Atlantic backing secret plotters

definitions.note: a collective noun for a group, so a singular word answers the plural plotters

indicators.note: backing means the whole run before it is read from right to left

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party

indicators.note: both sides of takes the first and last letters of the ocean's name

explanation.surface: The Labour party, in Britain and America alike, is supporting clandestine conspirators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides of' takes A and C from Atlantic; with LAB in front that is LABAC, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of people united in a clandestine intrigue.

clue.text: Corporation tardily expelling a Ted

indicators.note: expelling throws the two short words that follow out of the longer word

parts.note: belatedly means tardily, later than it should be
taken as written and run together

explanation.surface: A company slowly gets round to throwing out a man called Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelling' removes ATED from BELATEDLY. Corporation is an old humorous British word for a paunch, not the company the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is an old humorous word for a paunch or prominent stomach.

clue.text: Boast about getting clothing

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for boast is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about acquiring new clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a preposition, boasting about something, but it turns BRAG around; 'getting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A somewhat literary noun for dress or attire.

clue.text: A letter opener

definitions.meaning: the letter A is called this in the NATO radio spelling code
the first, or opening, letter of the Greek set of letters

explanation.definitionFit: It stands for A in radio spelling and is the first Greek character, the one that opens the series.

clue.text: Group, the members of which support divestment

definitions.text: Group, the members of which support divestment

parts.words: Group, the members of which support divestment
parts.note: divestment is read literally as the taking off of clothes, and the members are the paying patrons of such a venue

explanation.definitionFit: A venue whose paying patrons come to watch performers undress, which is divestment in its literal sense.

clue.text: Comfortable place with standards?

parts.note: a standard is a rose bush trained on a single tall stem, so a garden plot of them is also the proverbial easy situation

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an easy, pleasant situation, and literally a garden plot where standard bushes grow.

clue.text: Neat container of bay trees used at regular intervals

indicators.note: used at regular intervals means every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tidy planter holds bay trees spaced evenly apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy; it is an old word for cattle, so a neat container is a cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, and this is a British dialect word for a cowshed.
